Note from General Manager Community Safety

Staff have already reached out to the writer and advised that Engineering and Transportation will be reviewing the possibility of establishing a short-term drop-off zone in the area. This assessment will help address some of the immediate parking concerns raised.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to review traffic safety on Government Road
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is set to consider a traffic safety review for the Government Road area in Burnaby, prompted by resident reports of excessive speeding, aggressive driving, and street racing. Staff would study traffic speeds and volumes, review collisions and dangerous driving complaints, and coordinate with the RCMP on targeted enforcement. This is a proposed step — no new rules or changes have been approved yet. The review could lead to future speed limit changes, traffic-calming measures, road improvements, or increased police enforcement in the area.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and any follow-up public consultations — this could affect traffic and deliveries in your area.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to review Silver Ave drop-off zone and parking enforcement
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a report on parking and safety along Silver Ave after a parent was ticketed at Wonderworld Montessori Academy (6390 Silver Ave). The report covers a proposed 5-minute passenger loading/drop-off zone in front of the daycare, a review of meter enforcement timing during drop-off/pick-up windows, and confirms bylaw officers cannot investigate drug use—that's the RCMP's role. Council will decide on next steps, which could include new parking rules or enforcement changes for the street.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on Silver Ave—a new 5-minute drop-off zone could change curbside access for your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to review King and Park construction safety, skywalk
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is set to consider a report on traffic safety at the King and Park construction site. The pedestrian skywalk over Kingsway has been closed, and a resident has requested an immediate temporary pedestrian-actuated signal or rapid-flashing beacon at the old skywalk location, citing dangerous jaywalking. A permanent traffic light is planned but not until 2030. The community will be given a safe alternate route before the skywalk is removed. This is a proposed update, not a final decision.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on the King and Park skywalk and temporary signal — its outcome could affect pedestrian access near your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to review R1 SSMUH lot coverage rules for homeowners
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a request from homeowners Sean and Charlotte Nugent to review the R1 SSMUH lot coverage regulations, which took effect July 2026 and cap coverage at 40% of a lot. On their 4,002-square-foot lot, the existing 1,385-square-foot home leaves only 215 square feet for an accessory building — too narrow for a functional garage, forcing demolition and rebuild. The homeowners ask Council to exclude detached garages up to a reasonable size from lot coverage, grant extra coverage for accessory buildings on lots with existing homes, or create another mechanism. The proposal is not yet approved; if Council agrees, staff would review the rules and explain options like a Development Variance Permit (a formal request to bend zoning rules) or the Board of Variance (a panel that grants small exceptions). This could affect anyone building or expanding on an R1 lot in Burnaby.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for Council's decision on this review request — it could change what you can build on an R1 lot.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider recognizing Canadian Chinese Heritage Month
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will review a reply from federal Minister Marc Miller regarding a request to establish Canadian Chinese Heritage Month. The Minister notes federal designation requires a private Member's bill or House of Commons motion, and encourages the City to engage MPs and a senator. Council's review may lead to a future proclamation or recognition of the month in Burnaby. No decision has been made yet.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Battered Women's Support Services public safety report
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a report from Battered Women's Support Services (BWSS) on public safety, titled 'The Downplay Effect,' focused on the theme 'Public Safety Starts at Home.' The report asks the city to publicly commit to five priorities: mandate a municipal intimate partner violence (IPV) Task Force, advocate for a 15% increase in emergency funding for victim services and transition houses, strengthen local data collection, invest in prevention education, and appoint a dedicated IPV Lead. BWSS reports crisis calls from women increased 80% in the past 12 months. No decision has been made yet — this is an upcoming agenda item for discussion.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council meeting date and consider attending or submitting feedback on this public safety report.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby Council to consider Chemtrade extension request
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a request from Chemtrade for an extension of permitting chlorine production at its plant in the heart of Metro Vancouver, primarily for export to the US. A special report to Council on April 1, 2026 suggested the plant could be converted to produce bleach instead of the more toxic chlorine. The consultation period began in 2024. This is a proposed decision, not final. The extension could affect local businesses, especially those in industrial or related sectors, if approved.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Review the Chemtrade extension report and attend the council meeting or submit comments if your business may be affected.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to consider allowing one stairwell in 5-storey wooden buildings
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a proposal to allow 5-storey wooden buildings to have only one stairwell instead of the usual two. This change is part of a broader effort to reduce construction costs and increase housing options. If approved, it could affect new building designs and fire safety requirements. The proposal is still under review and has not been decided yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and public hearing dates if you are a developer or builder.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider: Dredging of Burrard Inlet correspondence
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a letter from Eagle Creek Streamkeeper Horațiu Halmaghi urging the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority to rescind the Burrard Inlet dredging proposal. The letter cites risks to wildlife, increased oil spill risk, and fossil fuel production, and argues the project assessment fails to address cumulative impacts of increased marine shipping. No decision has been made; Council will discuss whether to take action.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Monitor the council agenda for the outcome of this discussion — no immediate action is needed from business owners.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to implement provincial electric kick scooter pilot program
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is set to consider a report on Burnaby's implementation of the Provincial Electric Kick Scooter Pilot Program. Unlike the provincial framework that permits e-scooters on roads with speed limits of 50 km/h or less, Burnaby's proposed bylaw uses a more restrictive road-classification framework that prohibits e-scooters on major roads and arterials except where protected cycle lanes or multi-use pathways exist. A Transportation Committee member has asked Council to either amend the bylaw to align with the provincial framework or withdraw from the pilot. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Council decision on this pilot program — it could affect where scooters can operate in your area.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Rezoning at 7211 Greenford Avenue, Burnaby
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider first and second reading of Rezoning Bylaw No. 14839 (REZ #25-25) on July 28, 2026, to amend the CD Comprehensive Development District at 7211 Greenford Avenue. The amendment permits a six-storey, 142-unit low-rise apartment and a 27-storey tower with 276 market and non-market units, plus a two-storey commercial podium fronting Kingsway. No public hearing will be held; written comments are accepted.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Submit written comments referencing REZ #25-25 by email, webform, or mail before the July 28 Council meeting.
